title: Bélanger hydraulic jump
description: A stationary hydraulic jump on a horizontal frictionless bed: supercritical inflow (h1 = 0.2 m, Fr1 = 2.5) meets the Bélanger sequent depth h2 = 0.61 m held downstream. The exact solution is a step that stays at x = 50 m; the case checks that a solver captures the jump with the right conjugate depths and does not let it drift.

citations.title: Essai sur la solution numérique de quelques problèmes relatifs au mouvement permanent des eaux courantes (Bélanger sequent-depth relation)

criteria.rationale: Depth profile within 1 % (relative L1) of the stationary Bélanger step at x = 50 m on the finest grid. A captured jump smeared over two cells contributes Δh·2dx/L ≈ 0.5 % at dx = 0.25 m; a drifting jump or wrong sequent depth exceeds it.

Stored volume within 0.1 % of the exact step: a jump that drifts by half a cell (0.125 m) on the finest grid changes the volume by 0.13 %, so this fails any solver that cannot hold the Rankine–Hugoniot balance.
